title: errorbar
summary: Create plots with symmetric or asymmetric error bars using MATLAB-compatible `errorbar` forms.

gpu_support.notes: `errorbar` accepts resident floating inputs. Documented integer and logical inputs gather through their owning provider before the explicit client graphics conversion boundary; supported floating-vector combinations can use RunMat's direct geometry path.

description: `errorbar` visualizes uncertainty using vertical error bars with symmetric or asymmetric magnitudes. It returns graphics handles and follows MATLAB-compatible argument and property forms.
behaviors: Vertical, horizontal, and both-direction error-bar forms are supported through the runtime and replay/render stack.

Vector inputs create one error-bar handle. Matrix inputs create one registered error-bar series per plotted line; returning the complete handle vector remains limited by the current scalar graphics-handle builtin ABI.
All eight integer classes and logical coordinate/error arrays are accepted and cross one deliberate floating client-graphics boundary.
Cap size, line styling, marker appearance, display names, and related properties use the shared plotting object/property system.
Error bars remain subplot-local and integrate naturally with legends and axes state.
GPU-backed geometry is used only for compatible real floating vectors; integer, logical, matrix, and unsupported combinations gather to client plotting while preserving the same visible result.
Datetime, duration, categorical, distributed-array, and complete ErrorBar data-property compatibility remain development gaps.

examples.description: Style an error-bar object and label it for the legend

faqs.question: How do I plot asymmetric error bars?
Can I add horizontal error bars?
Can I combine error bars with a line or scatter plot?

gpu_residency: Real floating vectors can remain resident through RunMat's direct geometry path. Integer and logical buffers gather authoritatively before the client graphics conversion and are never reinterpreted as floating buffers.
gpu_behavior: Dedicated GPU geometry generation covers supported real floating-vector workflows; MATLAB documents errorbar gpuArray execution as client-side.
Markers continue to use the shared marker path so line/marker styling stays consistent with the rest of the plotting stack.
